solution.def: A homogeneous mixture: a solute (the dissolved substance) spread evenly through a solvent. In an aqueous solution, the solvent is water.

molarity.def: Concentration in moles of solute per liter of solution (mol/L, written M).

dilution.def: Making a solution weaker by adding solvent. The moles of solute stay the same, so M₁V₁ = M₂V₂, where V₂ is the final total volume.

volumetric-flask.def: A flask made to hold one exact volume, marked by a line on its neck; used with an analytical balance to prepare solutions of known molarity.

electrolyte.def: A solute whose aqueous solution conducts electricity because it contains moving ions. Strong electrolytes give many ions, weak ones few, nonelectrolytes none.
